overlayEntry.notes: Reviewed 2026-07-27 (replaces the 2026-07-20 review; measurements refreshed and the backstop gap resolved). K3's technical documentation establishes sBOLD as a standard-conforming ERC-4626 vault whose underlying asset is BOLD, deployed across Liquity V2 Stability Pools at pre-configured basis-point weights; collateral gains from liquidations are quoted in real time and swapped to BOLD through a SwapAdapter with a documented minimum-quantity formula (max slippage, reward and swap fee each capped at 10%), and deposit/withdraw preview rounding always favors the vault. Measured on-chain at Ethereum block 25627256 (2026-07-27T22:52:23Z) via eth_call: totalAssets() = 7,719,437.630014434 BOLD, totalSupply() = 7,176,569.116245205 sBOLD, convertToAssets(1e18) = 1.075644574 BOLD per share, and asset() confirms the underlying is BOLD (0x6440F144b7e50D6a8439336510312d2F54BeB01D). The wrapper originates no borrower debt and operates no collateral-ratio liquidation branches, so both CDP metrics and the collateralization and liquidation components remain structurally not applicable; liquidation execution is inherited from the parent BOLD system (variantOf bold-liquity, reviewed separately). BACKSTOP (adequate; newly graded): the wrapper itself adds no backstop and none is disclosed — the complete K3 documentation index (design, introduction, technical details, interactions, price oracle, audit reports, brand assets) and the deployed contract's function inventory contain no insurance, reserve, or recapitalization module — but sBOLD's deposits ride inside Liquity V2's per-branch Stability Pools, the parent's two-stage backstop of Stability Pool debt burn followed by same-branch redistribution. Measured from Liquity's own protocol stats API at 2026-07-27T22:56:39Z: total Stability Pool deposits of 20,879,166.75853167 BOLD against total BOLD supply of 29,607,199.86821610 give an inherited liquidation coverage of 70.5%, above the 0.658 level graded adequate for bold-liquity; the vault's on-chain sps() reads at block 25627256 confirm allocation into the three canonical Liquity V2 Stability Pools, providing the external on-chain anchor for the API figures. BRANCH ISOLATION (adequate; upgraded from limited): the prior review held that the configured weights were not published; K3's introduction page in fact documents the initial 60% wstETH / 30% WETH / 10% rETH allocation under biweekly admin rebalancing, and on-chain sps() reads at block 25627256 verify the live weights remain 30% WETH (pool 0x5721cbbd64fc7ae3ef44a0a3f9a790a9264cf9bf), 60% wstETH (pool 0x9502b7c397e9aa22fe9db7ef7daf21cd2aebe56b), 10% rETH (pool 0xd442e41019b7f5c4dd78f50dc03726c446148695). Liquity V2 keeps liquidation and redistribution losses within each collateral branch, but unrecovered bad debt in any branch transmits to the shared BOLD claim and hence to sBOLD's NAV, which prevents a strong rating. SHUTDOWN AND BAD DEBT (limited): K3's exchange-rate documentation conditions the compounding-share behavior on 'no bad debt from unsuccessful liquidations', i.e. unsuccessful-liquidation losses pass through to the share rate with no wrapper-level cure, and the parent Liquity V2 design has no unconditional recapitalization facility. STRUCTURAL REDEMPTION (limited): redemption is a standard ERC-4626 redeem, but the redeemed value depends on oracle-quoted collateral conversion executed by K3's mutable solver/swap infrastructure under admin control, and the interactions documentation states deposit and withdraw operations are restricted whenever accumulated collateral exceeds the configured maximum-collateral boundary, so redemptions can be temporarily gated under heavy liquidation flow. NOT ESTABLISHED: withdrawal behavior under Stability Pool withdrawal stress, the full admin/pause control inventory (verified source shows onlyOwner configuration setters plus pause/unpause), and any wrapper-level backstop (none documented or deployed).

collateralizationRatio.rationale: sBOLD is an ERC-4626 allocator over Liquity V2 Stability Pools; it originates no borrower debt and has no collateralized vault system of its own, so a system collateralization ratio is structurally undefined at the wrapper level.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: sBOLD has no debt of its own to offset; its deposits are themselves liquidation capital committed to the parent BOLD system, so a wrapper-level liquidation capacity ratio is structurally not applicable.

collateralizationParameters.rationale: The vault takes BOLD deposits and allocates them to Stability Pools; it has no borrower collateral positions or collateral-ratio thresholds.

liquidationMechanics.rationale: Liquidation execution is inherited from the parent Liquity V2 BOLD system; the wrapper only allocates deposits into Stability Pools and swaps accumulated collateral gains back to BOLD.

evidenceSummary: Replaced the 2026-07-20 entry with refreshed measurements and a resolved backstop gap. On-chain at Ethereum block 25627256 (2026-07-27T22:52:23Z, ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com): totalAssets() = 7,719,437.630014434 BOLD, totalSupply() = 7,176,569.116245205 sBOLD, convertToAssets(1e18) = 1.075644574 BOLD/share (vs 1.074291855 at block 25572100 on 2026-07-20), asset() = BOLD 0x6440F144b7e50D6a8439336510312d2F54BeB01D, and sps() reads show live weights 30% WETH / 60% wstETH / 10% rETH across the three canonical Liquity V2 Stability Pools. Backstop: no wrapper-level backstop exists or is disclosed (full K3 docs index + contract function inventory searched); the graded backstop is the inherited Liquity V2 two-stage mechanism — Liquity stats API fetched 2026-07-27T22:56:39Z shows 20,879,166.75853167 BOLD of Stability Pool deposits over 29,607,199.86821610 BOLD supply = 70.5% coverage, above the 0.658 adequate precedent, with the on-chain pool allocation as external anchor → backstop adequate. Branch isolation upgraded limited → adequate because the prior 'weights not published' premise was falsified (K3 documents the initial weights; live weights verified on-chain), matching the ybold-yearn wrapper precedent. shutdownAndBadDebt and structuralRedemption stay limited (losses pass through to share rate with no wrapper-level cure; redemption depends on K3's mutable swap infrastructure and can be gated by the max-collateral boundary). Both CDP metrics remain not-applicable per the wrapper's structure. Coordinator note: ybold-yearn (same parent, same wrapper pattern) carries the parent's CR/LCR as measured metrics while this entry keeps them not-applicable — a cross-entry consistency ruling may be wanted.
